answers.question: What is the Azure resource provider namespace and resource type of an Azure DocumentDB cluster?
answers.answer: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts

answers.question: Which Azure CLI command group creates and manages a cluster? Is it in the core CLI or an extension?
answers.answer: az cosmosdb (core CLI). Example: az cosmosdb create --name myAccount --resource-group myRG --kind MongoDB --locations regionName=westus2

answers.question: Which Bicep and Terraform resource types deploy a cluster?
answers.answer: Bicep: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts (and child types Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/mongodbDatabases and /mongodbCollections). Terraform (azurerm): azurerm_cosmosdb_account for the account, plus azurerm_cosmosdb_mongo_database and azurerm_cosmosdb_mongo_collection for MongoDB DBs/collections.

answers.question: What does a connection string look like: scheme, host suffix, port, and the options it must carry?
answers.answer: Standard MongoDB connection string. Example (direct): mongodb://<username>:<password>@<account>.mongo.cosmos.azure.com:10255/?ssl=true&replicaSet=globaldb&retryWrites=false&maxIdleTimeMS=120000. SRV form also works for supported accounts: mongodb+srv://<username>:<password>@<account>.mongo.cosmos.azure.com/?ssl=true&replicaSet=globaldb

answers.question: How is capacity provisioned and billed: request units, compute tiers with vCores, serverless, or something else?
answers.answer: Primary billing model is Azure Cosmos DB Request Units (RU/s) with provisioned throughput or serverless (pay-per-RU) where available. There is also a newer dedicated/vCore-style offering for some MongoDB-compatible SKUs (M-series) in some regions, but the common model is RU-based or serverless for Cosmos Mongo API.

answers.question: Which authentication methods are supported, and how does a driver authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID?
answers.answer: Data-plane access for the MongoDB API is typically done with MongoDB credentials (username/password) derived from the account keys and provided in the MongoDB connection string (SCRAM-based auth). Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) authentication is not generally supported for the MongoDB API data plane; drivers should use the connection string credentials and TLS.

answers.question: Which client library should an application use? Is there a service-specific SDK?
answers.answer: Use the official MongoDB drivers (for Python use pymongo). Do not use the Cosmos DB SQL/core SDK for MongoDB API workloads; the MongoDB wire protocol compatible drivers are the correct clients.

answers.question: Which vector index types are supported, and what does the command that creates one look like?
answers.answer: Index types include typical vector index families (example: hnsw, ivf, diskann) on vector-capable clusters. The MongoDB 7-style createIndex syntax is used. Example command: db.getCollection('profiles').createIndex({ embedding: 'knnVector' }, { name: 'vec_idx', dimensions: 1536, 'similarity': 'cosine', method: { name: 'hnsw', m: 16, efConstruction: 200 } })

answers.question: How are full-text search and hybrid search done?
answers.answer: Basic full‑text search can use MongoDB text indexes (db.collection.createIndex({field:'text'})). For richer/full-featured hybrid/vector+text search you typically combine vector queries with text filtering on the DB side or integrate with Azure Cognitive Search for advanced hybrid ranking; there is no separate built-in Cosmos 'hybrid search' engine for MongoDB API beyond text indexes and vector operators.

answers.question: Which MongoDB wire protocol or server versions are supported, and which commonly used MongoDB features are not?
answers.answer: Clusters advertise a MongoDB wire protocol version mapped to a server version (recent Cosmos Mongo API deployments support MongoDB 6.0 and 7.0 feature levels on newer clusters). However, not all MongoDB features are implemented identically; historically there have been gaps (some aggregation stages, server-side JS/eval, certain transaction semantics and advanced replication features). Expect to use standard drivers but validate advanced features (multi-shard transactions, some change-stream/aggregation behaviors) against the target cluster.

answers.question: How do you run the database locally for development and tests: which image or emulator, and which port?
answers.answer: There is no full emulator that perfectly reproduces the MongoDB API on Cosmos. For local development use the official MongoDB server Docker image (e.g. mongo:7.0) and expose port 27017: docker run -p 27017:27017 --name mongo -d mongo:7.0. For Cosmos-specific features test against a real Cosmos DB account since the emulator targets the SQL/core API only.

answers.question: Are change streams supported, and does anything have to be enabled first?
answers.answer: Change streams are supported when the cluster exposes a MongoDB wire protocol version that includes them; no special tenant toggle is normally required, but support has depended on the API/version of the account. In practice, use the driver's watch() API against the collection; if the account/version doesn't support change streams the driver will error.

answers.question: Which MCP server gives an agent data-plane tools for this service? Does the general Azure MCP Server cover it?
answers.answer: My expectation: the general Azure MCP/agents that manage Cosmos DB data-plane tasks are covered by the standard Azure management/control plane; there is not a separate special-purpose MCP server special-case for DocumentDB beyond the normal Azure management stack. (Low confidence — details vary by internal Microsoft infra.)

answers.question: What was this service called before, and how does it relate to Azure Cosmos DB and to the open-source DocumentDB project?
answers.answer: Azure DocumentDB was the original name of Microsoft's JSON document database service; it was rebranded/merged into Azure Cosmos DB. Cosmos exposes multiple APIs, one of which is the original DocumentDB/SQL API and another is the MongoDB-compatible API. The open-source DocumentDB project is unrelated; the Azure product is not the same as any separate open-source repository named DocumentDB.

answers.question: What engine is underneath, and does that change anything in application code?
answers.answer: Underneath is Microsoft/Azure's proprietary Cosmos DB engine implementing the MongoDB wire protocol for the MongoDB API. In most cases application code using standard MongoDB drivers will work, but expect behavioral and feature differences (throughput billed as RUs, some unsupported operators/stages, differences in transactions/consistency and certain admin commands). Test against the service to catch incompatibilities.

answers.question: Which database name should the sample use?
answers.answer: Use database name sample_banking_11 for all created collections and queries.

answers.question: Which environment variable contains the cluster connection string for this sample?
answers.answer: DOCUMENTDB_URI — read this at runtime (do not hard-code). Use it directly with MongoClient in the app.

answers.question: Which client library and commands will the sample use to create a vector index and run vector queries?
answers.answer: Use pymongo (official MongoDB Python driver). Create a vector index with collection.create_index({ 'embedding': 'knnVector' }, { 'dimensions': 1536, 'similarity': 'cosine', 'method': { 'name': 'hnsw', 'm': 16, 'efConstruction': 200 } }). Use find with $vectorSearch or the MongoDB 7 vector query operator to retrieve nearest neighbors.

answers.question: What collection schema and indexes will the sample create?
answers.answer: Create a collection 'profiles' in sample_banking_11. Documents include _id, name, metadata, embedding (array of floats, length 1536). Indexes: vector knnVector index on embedding (dimensions=1536, similarity=cosine, method=hnsw) and a text index on 'metadata' or 'adverse_media' fields for hybrid searches.

answers.question: How will the Python agent authenticate to the cluster in code?
answers.answer: Pass the DOCUMENTDB_URI connection string into pymongo.MongoClient(os.environ['DOCUMENTDB_URI'], tls=True). The connection string must include username/password and options like ssl=true and replicaSet=globaldb where required.
